comments.body:
## RCA — confirmed root cause (Phase 1 complete)

**Mechanism.** `compact_trigger._rebar_dir` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:48-50`)
derives every compaction sidecar as `os.path.dirname(tracker) + "/.rebar"` with NO symlink
resolution. A `make worktree` worktree's `.tickets-tracker` is a SYMLINK to the canonical
store while its `.rebar` is a real per-worktree directory, so `dirname()` stops at the
worktree and all three sidecars are keyed on the CALLER, not the store. Confirmed against the
existing contract `_store/lock.canonical_tracker` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py:150-153`):
"Resolve to a canonical path ... so symlinked and real-path callers contend on the SAME lock
file." The sibling `.rebar/hlc.lock` already resolves internally (`_store/hlc.py:80-83`), and
`_proc.detached_child_cwd` documents this exact worktree-symlink hazard.

**Runtime proof (dynamic claims, observed executing — not read off the source).** Two worktree
views of one canonical store, driven through the real functions:

```
lock path A      : <tmp>/wt-a/.rebar/compact-worker.lock
lock path B      : <tmp>/wt-b/.rebar/compact-worker.lock
paths equal      : False
acquire A        : True
acquire B        : 4          <-- BOTH held the "one compactor at a time" lock at once
canonical .rebar : <absent>   <-- nothing was ever created on the store
stale in B after A stamped a sweep : True   <-- B sees a store that has never swept
log path A       : <tmp>/wt-a/.rebar/logs/compact-worker.log
```

The exclusion the lock exists to provide does not hold: the second acquire returned a live fd
instead of `None`. That result also discriminates against the two rival explanations — that
`os.path.dirname` already normalises a symlinked path, and that the lock was store-scoped by
some other route — both of which predict `None` and a canonical lock file.

**Live evidence on this host:** 33 worktree-local `.rebar/compact-sweep.stamp` files and 33
worktree-local `.rebar/logs/compact-worker.log` files, and ZERO shared `compact-worker.lock`.
Every one of those stamps is a worktree that re-fires a store-wide sweep the store just had.

**What each artifact protects (established before moving any of them):**
* `compact-worker.lock` — mutual exclusion of compactor PROCESSES over one store
  (`:40` "one compactor at a time"). The proposition is about the store. Store-scoped.
* `compact-sweep.stamp` — written only by `compact.compact_all_cli` (`compact.py:617-622`)
  after a sweep of the shared tracker, and read by `_sweep_is_stale` to answer "does this
  STORE need a sweep". Nothing in the proposition mentions the worktree. Store-scoped, and
  its worktree-locality has the extra behavioural consequence the lock does not: a fresh
  worktree always reads maximally stale and re-fires a redundant store-wide sweep.
* `logs/compact-worker.log` — stderr of a detached child that sweeps the store and outlives
  the worktree that spawned it. Gitignored local diagnostics, but about the store; scattering
  it across removable worktrees destroys the only record of a failed sweep. Store-scoped.

No artifact here turned out to be genuinely per-worktree state.

**Legitimacy: `defect`.** The behaviour violates a cited design invariant stated in the code
itself (`:40` "one compactor at a time") and the store's explicit `canonical_tracker`
contract. Not a feature request: nothing new is being added, only the resolution that makes
the existing artifacts address what they were written to address.

**Defect origin — `caused_by` 1fde-becd-942a-4351 (gaudy-gangrenous-basilisk).**
`git blame -w -C -M -L 47,62` on the implicated lines names exactly one commit,
`d2dea317ec9405900c6769d8912e64b4624bfaf5` (2026-08-13, "Trigger compaction from the close,
out of band"), which ADDED the whole file — `rebar-ticket: 1fde-becd-942a-4351`. Date test
applied: `canonical_tracker` has existed since 57114212cf01 (2026-06-12), two months BEFORE
the implicated lines, so this is not an unmet obligation created by a later change — the
consumer failed an already-existing contract at birth, and there is no earlier point at which
the behaviour was right. Class: `plan_defect` — the derivation was copied verbatim from
`enrich_drain` ("as the drain uses"), inheriting the drain's missing resolution along with the
machinery it meant to reuse, and a reviewer of that story could have caught it.

**One correction to this ticket's description:** it states that `rebar doctor` "describes the
canonical `compact-worker.lock`". It does not — `doctor_locks.scan_locks` canonicalises
(`doctor_locks.py:328-329`) but its leg list is
`tickets-write-fcntl / tickets-write-mkdir / hlc / enrich-drain` (`doctor_locks.py:90-93`);
there is no compact-worker leg. The canonicalisation is still good evidence of the
store-scoped convention, but doctor does not currently report this lock at all. Not fixed
here (adding a doctor leg would be new capability, not restoration).

comments.body:
## Phase 2 complete — RED→GREEN, mutation-checked, landed for review

**Fix (restoration, not creation).** `compact_trigger._canonical_tracker` (new, lazy-import,
never-raises) resolves the tracker through symlinks via `_store.lock.canonical_tracker`, and
`_rebar_dir` now derives from the resolved path — so all three sidecars land on the CANONICAL
store's `.rebar/` and no caller can defeat the invariant. Second site in the same file:
`_spawn_detached_sweep` hands the detached child the canonical tracker (that argument also
becomes `run_sweep`'s `repo_root`, and the child outlives the worktree that spawned it; its
`cwd` was already resolved by `_proc.detached_child_cwd` for exactly this reason).

No new lock, no new protocol, no config key, no new caller-visible failure mode, no new
dependency, no weakened test. The lock stays non-blocking/best-effort.

**Contention analysis for the many-worktree case (~100 worktrees on this host).** The lock now
actually excludes, so the question is whether that introduces waiting. It does not: `_acquire_
trigger_lock` is `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` non-blocking and a loser simply returns `None`, so
`maybe_compact` declines to spawn and `run_sweep` returns — no blocking, no queue, no deadlock.
The change strictly REDUCES concurrent work: previously N worktrees could each run a store-wide
sweep against one store; now one does and the rest stand aside. The shared stamp removes the
redundant-sweep storm outright. No caller assumed the trigger was cheap-because-per-process —
the trigger's cost is the same two `O(1)` checks, and the only newly-shared cost is one `stat`
on a different path. The one new failure mode considered and rejected as a concern: a leaked
lock now suppresses the trigger store-wide rather than per-worktree — but that lock already
carries the v2 ownership stamp and is reclaimed by `lock_owner.stamped_file_is_stale`, the
exact discipline `knavish-stimulated-bluebottle` added, and `test_a_stale_worker_lock_is_
reclaimed` covers it.

**RED→GREEN.** Five new tests in `tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py`, authored BEFORE the fix
and held out of the fixer's tree (stashed to a patch; the fixer was given only the contract
card and told tests/ was off limits, and it verified against its own scratch script):
path invariance across two worktree views; real cross-worktree lock contention; stamp written
in A read in B (with a negative control asserting B reads stale beforehand); sidecars never
written into the worktree; detached child handed the canonical tracker. All five observed RED
for the right reasons first, all five GREEN after.

**Per-site mutation check — both hunks independently load-bearing.**
* Re-seed site 1 only (`_rebar_dir` loses the resolution): 4 failed, 15 passed — the argv test
  stayed green, so site 2 is not what makes those four pass.
* Re-seed site 2 only (argv back to the raw tracker): 1 failed, 18 passed — only the argv test
  went red, so site 1 is not what makes it pass.
* Fix restored: 19 passed.

**Replication of the original report.** The Phase-1 probe, re-run unchanged against the fixed
code: lock paths from both worktree views now equal and canonical, `paths equal: True`; the
second acquire returns `None`; `stale in B after A swept: False`; the log path is the canonical
store's. Both worktrees' `.rebar` stay empty; the canonical `.rebar` holds the lock.

**Gates.** `make lint` (ruff check + format-check, complexity ratchet `active=49 new=0
increased=0 stale=0`, config/env/DCO/criteria/skill gates, zizmor, actionlint) green;
`make typecheck` 616 files clean; the five repo-wide CI oracles the fast gates skip
(`check_wall_clock_asserts`, `check_raw_git_writes`, `check_comment_hygiene`,
`check_docs_index`, `check_config_reads`) all OK; full unit sweep **12077 passed, 44 skipped**.

**Step-7 sweeps.**
* *Construct axis.* Grepping the whole of `src/` for a tracker-derived `.rebar` sidecar finds
  exactly two other sites — `llm/enrich_drain.py:42` and `llm/overlap/queue.py:259` — both
  already fixed by the sibling `nuclear-calm-heron` change and both off-limits to this lane, so
  nothing left to fix. Every other `.rebar` path in the tree is `repo_root`-derived config
  (prompts, overlays, caches), which is legitimately per-clone and not a store sidecar.
* *Parity axis.* Rule: an artifact coordinating the ONE shared store must be keyed on the
  canonical store. Census — CLI `rebar compact-all` → `compact_all_cli` → `record_sweep`
  (`compact.py:617-622`): HOLDS via the fixed core. Scheduled workflow
  `.github/workflows/compact-sweep.yml` → same CLI: HOLDS. Close path
  `transition_close.py:358-360` → `maybe_compact`: HOLDS. Library `rebar.compact` /
  MCP `compact_ticket` → `compact_cli`, per-ticket and never a sweep (`compact_cli([])` is a
  usage error, so no surface can sweep without stamping): N/A. Read side (`_sweep_is_stale`,
  the storm-control probe): HOLDS by construction. One MISSING slot — `doctor_locks` has no
  `compact-worker` leg — filed as `bemused-painted-worm` (`8a0d-96ca-a60e-4da6`), linked
  `discovered_from` this bug, deliberately not fixed here because adding a doctor leg is new
  capability rather than restoration.

**Residual risk.** None observed beyond the doctor-leg gap above (ticketed). The stale-lock
blast radius change is analysed above and accepted: it is the intended consequence of the lock
becoming store-scoped, and it is already guarded by the shared staleness table.

**Also updated:** `docs/concurrency.md` now states that the worker lock, the sweep stamp and
the worker log live in the canonical store's `.rebar/`, so the doc no longer reads as if a
per-clone `.rebar` were correct.

**Gerrit change:** https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1994 (commit `a6a875d268`).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`_commands/compact_trigger._rebar_dir` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:47-50`)
carries the identical defect just proved and fixed for the enrichment drain in
`nuclear-calm-heron` (`da68-fc7c-068c-4c53`):

```python
def _rebar_dir(tracker: str) -> str:
    """The repo's ``.rebar/`` (sibling of the ``.tickets-tracker`` dir), as the drain uses."""
    return os.path.join(os.path.dirname(tracker), ".rebar")
```

It copied the drain's derivation verbatim ("as the drain uses", and the module header at
`:24-26` says the machinery is "REUSED from `rebar.llm.enrich_drain`") — including the
missing symlink resolution. A `make worktree` worktree's `.tickets-tracker` is a SYMLINK to
the canonical store while its `.rebar` is a real directory, so every compaction sidecar is
keyed on the worktree instead of the store:

* `compact-worker.lock` (`:52-53`) — annotated "Beside `enrich-drain.lock` in the repo's
  `.rebar/` — one compactor at a time" (`:40`). That intent is store-scoped and is not
  achieved: two worktrees take two different lock files while compacting the ONE store.
* `compact-sweep.stamp` (`:56-57`) — "records when a sweep last ran, so the trigger can fire
  on staleness alone". A per-worktree stamp means a fresh worktree always looks maximally
  stale, so it re-fires a sweep the store just had.
* `logs/compact-worker.log` (`:60-61`) — scattered and deleted with the worktree.

**Live evidence on this host: 33 worktree `.rebar/logs/compact-worker.log` files.** The
sweep has demonstrably been running with worktree-local sidecars.

The caller does not save it: `_commands/transition_close.py:360` passes `tracker` through
unresolved (contrast `_store/event_append.py:342` and `_store/push.py:484`, which both call
`_lock.canonical_tracker` before their drain hook).

## The contract being violated

`_store/lock.py:150-153` — `canonical_tracker`: *"Resolve to a canonical path … so symlinked
and real-path callers contend on the SAME lock file."* The neighbouring `.rebar/hlc.lock`
already resolves internally (`_store/hlc.py:80-83`), and `_commands/doctor_locks.py:328-329`
already canonicalises before reporting lock legs — so `rebar doctor` describes the canonical
`compact-worker.lock` while the sweep in a worktree takes a different one.

## Scope

Same shape as the drain fix: resolve inside the path derivation
(`compact_trigger._rebar_dir`) via `_lock.canonical_tracker`, so the invariant cannot be
defeated by a caller. Keep the lazy-import posture and the never-raise posture.

Filed separately rather than folded into `nuclear-calm-heron`: different feature
(compaction, not enrichment), different file lane (`_commands/` not `llm/`), and a distinct
third artifact (the sweep stamp) whose worktree-locality has a behavioural consequence — a
redundant sweep — that the drain's lock and log do not have.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Two worktree views of one store derive the SAME `compact-worker.lock` path, under the
      canonical store's `.rebar`, and contend on it (second acquire refused).
- [x] `compact-sweep.stamp` written from one worktree is READ by another worktree of the
      same store, so a fresh worktree does not re-fire a sweep the store just had.
- [x] `compact-worker.log` from a worktree-spawned sweep lands on the canonical store and
      survives the worktree's removal.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the complexity ratchet and the full unit sweep are green.

RED->GREEN oracle for cross-worktree lock contention, stamp sharing and sidecar durability
